obligations.obligation: Public integrations target owned language bindings or declared face projections, never the engine.
obligations.mutation: Document a caller integration that invokes an engine class directly.

obligations.obligation: Contracts determine binding behavior and engine obligations; implementation disagreements are defects.
obligations.mutation: Revise a frozen promise solely to match an existing implementation.

obligations.obligation: No binding is authoritative and engine coupling stays an owned replaceable detail.
obligations.mutation: Adopt Python behavior as the rule or publish its private transport as the product interface.

obligations.obligation: Do not offer a supported amplifier-agent command interface.
obligations.mutation: Ship an agent invocation CLI for applications to script against.

obligations.obligation: Distinguish normative contracts from guides and vision; preserve the ability to replace the engine.
obligations.mutation: Use a guide-only option to override a frozen exclusion or freeze an engine-language type.

obligations.obligation: Compatibility evidence includes the spec, discriminating kit, passing implementation, and a usable worked example.
obligations.mutation: Claim compatibility from the freeze date alone with no executed public scenarios.

obligations.obligation: Agent-interface and event compatibility require Python plus an independently written non-Python binding.
obligations.mutation: Report a generated Python port as independent implementation evidence.

obligations.obligation: Internal-boundary verification uses the public kits it serves, not its own mechanism-specific certification harness.
obligations.mutation: Create a seam protocol compatibility suite that substitutes for public binding tests.

obligations.obligation: A freeze depends on an owner-ratified dated changelog entry, not descriptive prose.
obligations.mutation: Treat a heading containing FROZEN as owner ratification without a dated entry.

obligations.obligation: Runtime compatibility scenarios invoke public APIs against a scripted provider that is private to the kit.
obligations.mutation: Assert internal queue contents or use live model output as deterministic contract evidence.

obligations.obligation: The kit includes static surface checks and repeats scenarios after engine replacement with new sessions.
obligations.mutation: Run only runtime happy paths or substitute a new provider for engine replacement.

obligations.obligation: Contract version identifiers are independent of releases and no additional seam protocol version is exposed.
obligations.mutation: Require package-version equality in place of public contract compatibility.

obligations.obligation: Within a major, amendments preserve existing fields/types/defaults and do not add mandatory requirements without absorption evidence.
obligations.mutation: Make an optional field required without evidence existing consumers accept it.

obligations.obligation: Preserve unknown optional data and owned extensions; adding a registered event requires a contract amendment.
obligations.mutation: Register a new unqualified event as an implementation-only change.

obligations.obligation: Breaking changes use a separate major-version file with a stated dual-serving window.
obligations.mutation: Replace v1 signatures in place without publishing a coexistence window.

obligations.obligation: Backlogged and reserved items gain no guarantee merely because a trigger is met.
obligations.mutation: Treat media or sub-agent lifecycle events as mandatory without a ratified amendment.

obligations.obligation: Divergent implementation work follows its governing amendment and work items rather than retroactive documentation.
obligations.mutation: Land a new public option and amend its governing contract afterward.

obligations.obligation: Owner-ratified CANDIDATE amendments require evidence of a break, cost, or platform limitation.
obligations.mutation: Change a frozen clause based solely on developer preference.

obligations.obligation: Fix implementation defects toward the contract; divergence requires explicit governance rather than convenience.
obligations.mutation: Weaken cancellation semantics because the selected provider adapter cannot deliver them.

obligations.obligation: Contract amendments update body and dated changelog together; contract text does not record implementation progress.
obligations.mutation: Change the body without its dated decision or insert an implementation status section.

obligations.section: House rules, inherited by every contract
obligations.obligation: Failures identify an actionable remedy and never present degraded, partial, or fabricated results as success.
obligations.mutation: Return an apology as a successful completion after provider failure.

obligations.section: House rules, inherited by every contract
obligations.obligation: Configuration, event types, and error codes use registered sets; extensions use owned keys and unknown unqualified names are refused.
obligations.mutation: Accept an unqualified custom event or silently ignore an unsupported configuration key.

obligations.section: House rules, inherited by every contract
obligations.obligation: Caller contracts and surfaces conceal replaceable engine internals.
obligations.mutation: Expose engine composition or transport fields in public records.

obligations.section: House rules, inherited by every contract
obligations.obligation: Conversation state stays caller-side; default retention is off and provider state is never necessary for continuation.
obligations.mutation: Require provider response history to resume after restarting all processes.

obligations.section: House rules, inherited by every contract
obligations.obligation: Named exclusions receive static enforcement; behavioral exclusions receive amendment review and have no promotion path.
obligations.mutation: Promote an excluded behavior using a backlog trigger or claim name scanning proves behavioral absence.
